newsitem.title: USA: Florida Supreme Court approves Tampa Bucs bonds.
newsitem.headline: Florida Supreme Court approves Tampa Bucs bonds.

text.p: Florida's Supreme Court Thursday sided with backers of the beleaguered Tampa Bay Buccaneers and approved the sale of $204 million of revenue bonds to finance a new football stadium.

In a unanimous unsigned opinion, Florida's highest court reversed a lower court ruling that said local officials overstepped their authority by agreeing to build the stadium to keep the professional football team from moving to another city.
The NFL team, which has the worst overall team record in league history, had threatened to leave the city unless an improved stadium is built by January 1, 2000.
Last fall, Hillsborough County voters approved a referendum raising sales taxes to pay for the stadium and other projects.
Along with revenues from their own games, the Bucs would receive some revenues from non-Bucs events at the arena ranging from college football games to tractor pulls.

Former Tampa Mayor Bill Poe filed suit arguing that the city-financed stadium improvements were unconstitutional because they benefited a private business at public expense. In March, a local circuit judge agreed.
In its 10-page ruling Thursday, the high court reversed that ruling, saying that regardless of the wisdom of the endeavor, the voters had spoken.
If voters are unhappy with the referendum, they can take it out on local politicians at the ballot box when those officials come up for re-election, the court said.

"Indeed, as noted earlier, the majority of citizens voting on the bond issue, while apparently aware of the obvious benefits of the deal to the Bucs ownership, nevertheless voted to go forward," the court said. "Only time will tell if the policy choices made here were wise ones."

Attorneys representing the City of Tampa, Hillsborough County and the Tampa Sports Authority argued earlier this month that the team brings an estimated $3 billion a year into the local economy, a figure that far outweighs any financial gain experienced by Bucs owners.
The bonds are to be issued by the stadium authority.
